title: Keep the relay password out of the logs

blocks.text: The notification service sends mail through a relay described by `SmtpSettings`. It logs the settings at start-up, and every delivery error carries the delivery job, a record that holds the settings, so that the on-call engineer can see which relay and account failed. Those errors get pasted into tickets, and a reviewer has noticed that a ticket shows the relay's password.

Write `toString()` in `src/main/java/practice/SmtpSettings.java`. The engineer still needs the host, the port and the user, in the settings and in any record that holds them; nothing of the password may show, not even its first few characters. About two lines in total.

cases.says: the settings print their host, port and user
a record that carries the settings prints which relay and user it used
the password appears neither in the settings' printed form nor in that of a record carrying them
no part of the password, such as its first characters, appears in the printed settings

origin.section: A Record's toString Prints Every Component, Password Included

concepts: A record's generated toString prints every component, so log calls, exception messages and enclosing records print a password component.
A redacting toString keeps the non-secret components and shows nothing of the secret, so an enclosing record's generated toString is safe too.
